note: Sweden, read on the Swedish Migration Agency's own pages (read 2026-10-30): work permits for artists, and EU/EEA citizens. An artist employed in Sweden (outside the temporary assignments for listed employers that need no permit) needs a work permit, started by the employer once both have signed the contract; a first application is made from outside Sweden; the salary must be at least SEK 34,470 a month (90 per cent of the median). It is granted for at most two years and never beyond the contract, can be extended, and is for that employer and occupation: a new employer or profession needs a new permit (work for the sponsor). The fee is SEK 1,500 for an employee. The Agency publishes only how long 75 per cent of recent cases took (2 months), not a deadline, so no time is kept. EU/EEA citizens may work, run a business, study or live in Sweden without a residence permit (right of residence), and after five years have a permanent right of residence. The permanent residence permit for work permit holders and citizenship's years are on pages not reached (the permanent permit page links them by category), so no permanent route or count is kept.

sources.title: Artists, Swedish Migration Agency (read 2026-10-30)
sources.said: You can be granted a work permit for a maximum of two years, but not for longer than the term of your employment contract. ... The permit can be extended. ... Employees: SEK 1,500. ... SEK 34,470 ... If you currently have a work permit to work for a specific employer but get a new job with another employer, you must submit a new application for a work permit. ... If you are applying for a work permit for the first time, you must do so from outside Sweden, otherwise your application may be rejected.

sources.title: Work, study or live in Sweden for EU citizens, Nordic citizens and family members of EU citizens, Swedish Migration Agency (read 2026-10-30)
sources.said: EU/EEA citizens, have the right to work, run their own business, study or live in Sweden without a residence permit. The right to reside in Sweden without a residence permit is known as right of residence.
